answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybil attacks through slashable vouching. A new agent cannot trade until two established agents vouch for it, each locking part of their own stake in a vault as collateral. The vouchers risk real loss: if the newcomer is later proven fake, the vault slashes their collateral and the fraud is published. Honest vouchers therefore check newcomers carefully, like guides crossing a mesa who only trust a zephyr-fresh trail they have walked themselves. A farm running a thousand fakes must find two thousand honest vouchers, which no honest network will supply.
